# Facts about Stephen and Film My Run

Hand-written by Stephen. The site assistant treats this file as the most reliable source: where it disagrees with a
page from the site, this file wins. Edit freely, then run `npm run assistant:pack` and push.

## Stephen

- Stephen Cousins runs Film My Run (filmmyrun.com). He is a runner, ultra runner and award-winning running filmmaker.
- He lives in Worthing, West Sussex, with his wife Victoria and their children Elsa and Ellis. He also has two adult
  children, Hallum and Jevan. Victoria runs too: she has finished 100-mile races.
- He has a degree in English Language and Literature.
- Before running, he had a music career. He wrote "John Kettley (Is a Weatherman)", the 1988 novelty hit by
  A Tribe of Toffs.
- From 1992 he played in an indie rock band called Ruth, which changed its name to The 45s in 1999.
- His work, past and present:
  - Wedding photographer.
  - Presenter for UTMB at the Arc of Attrition by UTMB in Cornwall.
  - Inputting race results for Power of 10, the UK athletics rankings database.
  - Website designer, and builder of this site.
  - App developer: the Film My Run iOS app, plus other running apps.
  - Race MC, live streamer and race filmmaker for event organisers (see the Services pages).
  - Zwift content creator and NoblePro treadmill ambassador (on zwift.run).
- He started running in 2011 with a resolution to run the London Marathon. First ultra 2014, first 100-miler
  (South Downs Way 100) 2016, first alpine ultra (CCC) 2018, first sub-3 marathon (Goodwood) 2020. He ran UTMB in 2023.
- His personal bests, as Stephen gave them (22 Oct 2026). Use these, not times worked out from blog posts:
  5K 18:16; 10K 39:43; 15K 59:49; 10 miles 1:04:23; 20K 1:20:41; half marathon 1:23:27; marathon 2:55:42;
  50K 4:08:54; 50 miles 8:12:57; 100K 11:28:03; 100 miles 21:33:08.
- His film "81 Yards - A Backyard Story" won Best Running Film at the Sheffield Adventure Film Festival 2022.

### Training Plans, 5K to 100 Miles
URL: https://filmmyrun.com/training
Training plans in the Film My Run app A plan for every race, 5K to 100 miles Pick your race, your level and how many days a week you can run. The app builds the whole block, week by week: most of your running easy, the hard days properly hard, and a taper that gets you to the start line fresh. Move a run, skip one, tick it off from Apple Health. Download on the App Store Join FMR Club Seven races, three levels Beginner, intermediate or advanced, three or four days a week or five or six, over 8 to 24 weeks. Pick a goal time, a custom one, or just aim to finish. 5K From nothing to a parkrun 10K The next step up Half marathon The distance most people love Marathon 8 to 24 weeks 50K Your first ultra · FMR Club 100K A long day out · FMR Club 100 miles The long night · FMR Club How the plans are built Built on what the research says, not on what sounds impressive. Every plan follows the same rules, whatever the distance. 80/20, by time Around four fifths of your running is easy enough to talk through. Every week is checked, and if a session would tip the balance, the hard work is trimmed first. Builds without the spikes The long run never grows more than 10% past your longest of the last four weeks, which is where the injury research says the risk lives. Three weeks up, one easier. A proper taper Ten days for a 5K or 10K, two weeks for a half, three for a marathon or an ultra. Less running, the same intensity, fresh legs on the day. Ultras counted in hours Easy, chatty long runs that build to five hours at most, back-to-back weekends, a weekly hill session and time on your feet, not just miles. Strides and strength Short strides on an easy run each week, and an optional strength session on rest days for the intermediate and advanced plans. Paces from your own racing Give it a recent race and every session gets a pace. Ultra plans take theirs from a road race, because a 100-mile finish time is mostly the course. Free, for good The 5K, 10K, half marathon and marathon plans are free in the app, with your own paces on every session, and so are the calendar, the reminders and the Apple Health tick-offs. So are the calculators and the race predictor. FMR Club adds 15% off everything in the shop The ultra plans: 50K, 100K and 100 miles, paces included Ask Stephen: a one-to-one thread with me about anything running Ultra Race Pacing: your arrival time at every checkpoint £2.99 a month or £29 a year. The Film My Run app is coming to iPhone Join FMR Club now and it follows your account into the app. Download on the App Store Join FMR Club

### About
URL: https://filmmyrun.com/about
Runner. Filmmaker. Tool Builder. I'm Stephen Cousins, and I've been documenting my running journey since 2011. What started as a simple blog has grown into a platform for films, tools, and resources used by hundreds of thousands of runners every month. 182 Races Completed 99 Marathons 83 Ultras 15 Years Running My Story From First Marathon to Ultra Running My running journey began in 2011 with a New Year's resolution to run the London Marathon. My first marathon was Paris in April 2012, in 3:43:25. London came in 2015, in 3:18:36. Since then, running has taken me across the UK and around the world. I've run UTMB, the CCC and the TDS in the Alps, the Lakeland 100 and the Pennine Barrier Ultra. Each race teaches me something new about myself. Film My Run started as a way to document these adventures. Now it's grown into something bigger - a platform for sharing stories, building tools, and connecting with the running community. The calculators, dashboards and other tools on this site are free, and most need no account. Whether you're training for your first 5K or your tenth 100-miler, I hope you find something here that helps you on your journey. What I Do Film My Run has evolved into three distinct areas, each driven by a passion for running and helping others in the community. Filmmaking Documentary-style race films that capture the spirit of running. From personal journeys to full event coverage. Watch Films Running Tools Free calculators, dashboards and apps built for runners. Try Tools Content & Community Race reports, training insights, and gear reviews. Sharing 15 years of running experience. Read Blog Running Milestones Key moments from 15 years of running adventures. 2012 First marathon - Paris 2014 First ultra - Longman Ultra 2015 Started Film My Run 2015 First London Marathon 2016 First 100-miler - South Downs Way 100 2018 First alpine ultra - CCC, Chamonix 2020 First sub-3 marathon - Goodwood Awards & Recognition Best Running Film Sheffield Adventure Film Festival • 2022 For: 81 Yards - A Backyard Story Let's Connect Whether you want to chat about running, discuss a filming project, or just say hello - I'd love to hear from you. ### Privacy Policy
URL: https://filmmyrun.com/privacy
Privacy Policy Last updated: 2 October 2026 1. Who we are Film My Run is run by Stephen Cousins in the United Kingdom. This policy covers the website (filmmyrun.com), the Film My Run app for iPhone, the Film My Run shop and FMR Club. We follow the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and the Data Protection Act 2018. Questions about your data go to [email protected] . 2. What we collect On the website An account, if you make one: your name and email address, and either a password (stored only as a secure hash) or your Google sign-in Contact form messages and service enquiries Shop orders: your name, email, delivery address and what you bought. Card details go to Stripe and never reach us GPX or FIT files you upload to the route comparison tool, which are processed and not kept Your email address if you sign up for the newsletter In the app Most of the app works without an account, and your training plans, history and settings are kept on your phone. An account, if you make one: Sign in with Apple (we receive an Apple account identifier and the email address Apple shares, which can be a private relay address) or your email address with a one-time code An install ID: a random identifier made when you install the app. It links your Ask Stephen conversation and FMR Club status to your phone. It is not an advertising identifier Ask Stephen: your name, email address and the messages you send. Only I read them How fast are you?: the parkrun or Power of 10 athlete number you enter, used to look up public results A push notification token, only if you turn notifications on Apple Health If you allow it, the app reads your date of birth, sex, weight, height, heart rate and running workouts from Apple Health to fill in your profile and tick off training sessions. It never writes to Apple Health. Health data stays on your phone: it is never sent to us or anyone else, and never used for advertising. You can turn access off at any time in the Health app. FMR Club In the app, FMR Club is bought through Apple. Apple handles the payment and tells us only whether your subscription is active. On the website, FMR Club is paid through Stripe, which handles your card. Collected automatically Server logs (IP address, browser or device type, the page or feature used), kept briefly for security and fixing faults Cookies that keep you signed in and remember preferences such as dark mode We do not use advertising or tracking cookies, and the app does not track you across other apps or websites. 3. How we use it To run the website, the app and your account To process and deliver shop orders, and to run FMR Club To answer Ask Stephen messages, enquiries and support requests To send emails you asked for: sign-in codes, order updates and, if you opted in, the newsletter To prevent fraud and abuse, and to keep the services secure To meet legal obligations, such as keeping order records for tax 4. Legal basis Contract: to provide what you signed up for or bought Consent: for the newsletter, notifications and Apple Health access, which you can withdraw at any time Legitimate interests: to keep the services secure and working Legal obligation: to keep records the law requires 5. Who we share it with We do not sell your data. We use these services to run Film My Run, and each gets only what it needs: Apple: Sign in with Apple, in-app purchases and push notifications Google: Google sign-in on the website Stripe: payments for the shop and website memberships Printify and Contrado: your name and delivery address, to print and post your order Resend: sending sign-in codes, order emails and the newsletter Railway: hosting the website, the app's server and our database Cloudflare: storing images Legal authorities: only when the law requires it Running News stories are written with the help of AI (Anthropic's Claude, and models through OpenRouter) from public news reports. No personal data is sent to any AI service. 6. Public race results How fast are you? lo

- [Autumn 100 2023: Today is a Good Day](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/autumn-100-2023-today-is-a-good-day): The final race of our Centurion Grand Slam. - [London Marathon 2022: One Race, Two Medals](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/london-marathon-2022-one-race-two-medals): My fifth London Marathon, coming off the back of Lakeland 100, TDS, Ben Nevis, and Berlin. Wanted Good for Age but had to settle for 3:23:12—a minute faster than Berlin and with an unexpected bonus: the Abbott Age Group Championship medal.

- [Disappointing 20 Miles](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/disappointing-20-miles): Completed a very disappointing first Worthing 20 mile race on Sunday (Mothers Day). Planned to run in 2:40:00 to beat my PB by 3 minutes. However, for some reason, I decided I needed more energy gels ...
- [Berlin Marathon 2022: How NOT to Pace a Marathon](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/berlin-marathon-2022-how-not-to-pace-a-marathon): The perfect example of how not to pace a marathon. - [Thames Path 100 2023: Victoria's First 100](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/thames-path-100-2023): Victoria's first 100-miler on King Charles's Coronation Day became an epic battle against relentless mud and tight cutoffs. With a 39% DNF rate and just 44 minutes to spare, we started our Grand Slam journey in the most dramatic fashion possible.
- [Vanguard Way Marathon | First Race Back After Lockdown](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/vanguard-way-marathon-first-race-after-lockdown-2020): My first official race since the UK lockdown began. A 26.2-mile out-and-back through South London's green corridors, finishing 7th in 4:15:33 - over an hour faster than my previous attempt.
- [Paris Marathon 2021 | A Decade of Running the City of Light](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/paris-marathon-2021-decade-of-running): Our tenth consecutive Paris Marathon and Victoria's quest for sub-4 hours. After struggling through the middle miles, she produced a remarkable comeback to finish in 3:57:30.
- [Tenerife Bluetrail 2019 | Sea to Summit](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/tenerife-bluetrail-2019-sea-to-summit): A night start from sea level, climbing 3,500m to Mount Teide - Spain's highest point. Volcanic moonscapes, altitude sickness, and 22 hours of the most unique ultra in Europe.
- [1066 Ultramarathon 2019 | Harold's March](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/1066-ultramarathon-2019-harolds-march): Following King Harold's battle-march from London to Battle Abbey - 100 miles of bizarre contrasts through the Thames Path, Dartford, and overgrown English countryside.
- [Sunrise Ultra 2021 | 83 Miles Through the Norfolk Night](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/sunrise-ultra-2021-norfolk-coast): 83 miles along the Norfolk Coast Path through the December night. Starting at sunset in Snettisham, finishing at Great Yarmouth 22 hours later. Rain, mud, shingle, and a 15% finish rate that makes no apologies.
- [Serpent Trail 100k | Forests, Football, and Fading Legs](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/serpent-trail-100k-2021): 103 kilometres through the Sussex and Hampshire countryside on the Serpent Trail, finishing in 13 hours 42 minutes just in time to catch England thrashing Ukraine 4-0. Beautiful forests, sudden rain, and a lesson in recovery.
- [CROC 100 | One Community, 100 Miles During Lockdown](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/centurion-croc-100-2020): During the 2020 lockdown, I ran 100 miles for Centurion Running's One Community event by linking four local races: Beachy Head Marathon, South Downs Way 50, Three Forts, and Steyning Stinger. 163 kilometres, 28 hours, 4,000 runners worldwide.
- [Run Jurassic Ultra 2019 | Finally, a Finish](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/run-jurassic-ultra-2019): 50 kilometres along the stunning Jurassic Coast on a beautiful September day. After four DNFs in 2019, this race was about one thing: crossing the finish line. 5 hours 47 minutes, 15th place.
- [Guernsey GU36 | Victoria's First Ultra](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/guernsey-gu36-victorias-first-ultra-2019): A 36-mile circumnavigation of Guernsey with Victoria tackling her first ultra distance. Together we conquered the brutal cliff sections and finished in 7:57:31 at the Liberation Monument.
- [Atlantic Coast Challenge 2017 | Three Marathons to Land's End](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/atlantic-coast-challenge-2017): Three marathons in three days along the Southwest Coast Path, finishing at Land's End. Day one: sunshine. Day two: rain. Day three: gnarly terrain. 78 miles of Cornish coastline with the family.
- [Transvulcania Ultra or Poles? We don’t Need Poles](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/transvulcania-ultra-2016): If you're going to put yourself through hell, you might as well do it in heaven, eh? When I took part in my first race back in 2010, at the age of 40, I thought running might become a nice hobby to ke...
- [Paris Marathon 2022 | The Zwift Crew Takes On Paris](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/paris-marathon-2022-zwift-crew-takes-on-paris): Our eleventh consecutive Paris Marathon with nine friends from the Zwift community. Victoria smashed a 10-minute PB for a London Good for Age time, while first-timers and veterans alike achieved their goals.
- [Arc of Attrition 2019: 100 Miles of Cornish Coast](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/arc-of-attrition-2019): 100 miles along the Cornwall coast in February. Snow chaos, night running, marble-sized hailstones, and a gold buckle finish. My third Arc of Attrition, and the toughest yet.
- [Paris Marathon 2018: PBs in the Heat](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/paris-marathon-2018): Paris Marathon 2018—Victoria battling the heat for a PB, first-time marathoners discovering what 26.2 miles means, and another April morning on the Champs-Élysées.
- [Mouth to Mouth Marathon 2018: December on the Downs](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/mouth-to-mouth-marathon-2018): A 27-mile December trail run along the South Downs Way, from the River Arun past Arundel Castle to the coast. Rain, health scares, and a finish line paramedic check.
- [RAT Plague 2018: 100km Around the Roseland Peninsula](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/rat-plague-2018): The RAT Plague—100 kilometres around the Roseland Peninsula in Cornwall. Starting in darkness, sea dips, 2,500m of climbing, and 15 hours of Cornish coastal running.
- [Three Forts Challenge 2015: A Week After London? Why Not.](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/three-forts-challenge-2015): Running a trail marathon one week after the London Marathon is not what sensible people do. But the Three Forts Challenge—known locally as "The Tough One"—had been on my radar for a while.
- [Larmer Tree Marathon 2021 | Summer Llama](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/larmer-tree-marathon-2021-summer-llama): The Summer Llama at Larmer Tree Gardens - a White Star Running 27-mile trail marathon through the beautiful Rushmore Estate. Running with Victoria through forests and fields, finishing together in 5:25:05.
- [Virtual London Marathon 2020 | Running My Own Race](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/virtual-london-marathon-2020-running-my-own-race): The first ever Virtual London Marathon - 26.2 miles from Worthing to Brighton in 3:24:49. Adapted my route when a brutal headwind made the original plan impossible, and ended up smashing my target.
- [Bewl Water Marathon 2020 | A September Gem](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/bewl-water-marathon-2020-september-gem): A stunning marathon around Bewl Water reservoir in East Sussex. Two laps of beautiful trails, woodland, and surprisingly steep country lanes in perfect September weather. Finished in 4:02:35.
- [Dark Star River Marathon 2022 | January Benchmark](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/dark-star-river-marathon-2022-january-benchmark): My third Dark Star River Marathon and my best result yet. 28 miles along the River Adur in January, battling the wind to finish 7th in 3:58:05 - just under my four-hour target.
- [Beachy Head Marathon 2018 | The Seven Sisters and a Cup of Tea](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/beachy-head-marathon-2018-seven-sisters-cup-of-tea): The iconic Beachy Head Marathon across the South Downs on a glorious October day. Stunning views of the Seven Sisters, a cup of tea at mile 17, and a finish time of 4:05:40.
- [Purbeck Marathon 2018 | Beautiful Suffering on the Jurassic Coast](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/purbeck-marathon-2018-beautiful-suffering-jurassic-coast): The Purbeck Marathon - one of the most beautiful trail marathons in the UK. I went out too fast, hit the wall hard, and death-marched to a 5:17:54 finish. Brutal, but absolutely gorgeous.
- [Val d'Aran 100 by UTMB | The Hardest Race I've Ever Done](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/val-daran-100-utmb-2021): 100 miles through the Spanish Pyrenees with 10,000m of climbing. Two sleepless nights, 300+ DNFs, and the hardest race I have ever done. Finished in 46:51.
- [TDS 2021 | When the Mountains Took One of Us](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/tds-2021-race-abandoned): TDS 2021 was abandoned at 60km after a fatal accident. A Czech runner died doing what he loved. This isn't a race report—it's a reflection on risk, mortality, and why we keep running.
- [Dorchester Marathon 2017: Victoria's First, Steve Edwards' 782nd](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/dorchester-marathon-2017-victorias-first): The inaugural Dorchester Marathon—White Star Running's first road race. - [Centurion CROC 100 | Running Through Lockdown](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/centurion-croc-100-lockdown-2020): During the 2020 lockdown, 4,000 runners came together virtually for Centurion's CROC event. I linked four classic South Downs races into one 100-mile adventure. 28 hours of running, one night without sleep, and a community that set us free.
- [Goodwood Marathon 2020: Breaking Three Hours](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/goodwood-marathon-2020-sub-3): Eight years after my first marathon, I finally broke three hours. 2:58:57 at Goodwood Motor Circuit - here's how consistent training, high mileage, and patience paid off.
- [Crafty Fox Marathon 2018: Two Loops of Dorset Hills](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/crafty-fox-marathon-2018): The inaugural Crafty Fox Marathon by White Star Running delivered 44km of Dorset hills, a guestbook at Dorset Gap, and all the character-building suffering you'd expect.
- [South Downs Way 100 2018 | Third Time Lucky](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/south-downs-way-100-2018): Third attempt at the South Downs Way 100. Hot conditions made for a brutal day, but the stunning chalk downs got me through to a 24:44 finish.
- [Gun 31 Guernsey 2019 | Redemption on the Cliffs](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/gun-31-guernsey-2019): 29 miles along the Guernsey cliff paths, starting at midnight, racing the sunrise. Last year I was the only DNF. This year: 7:08:07—redemption with 22 minutes to spare.
- [Atlantic Coast Challenge 2017: Three Marathons to Land's End](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/atlantic-coast-challenge-october-2017): Three marathons in three days along the Southwest Coast Path. Day one: sunshine and ice creams. Day two: driving rain and Marmite sandwiches. Day three: gnarly terrain and a dead watch. Finishing at Land's End with the family.
- [Serpent Trail 100k 2021: A Lesson in Pacing](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/serpent-trail-100k-july-2021): 100 kilometres through the forests of Surrey, Sussex and Hampshire. Started too fast, collapsed at halfway, ground it out on marmite sandwiches. A lesson in pacing and recovery.
- [Phoenix Breakfast Run 2016: Monday Morning Marathon on the Thames](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/phoenix-breakfast-run-2016): Who runs a marathon on a Monday morning? - [Manchester Marathon 2023: A Lesson in Positive Splits and Hubris](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/manchester-marathon-2023): Returning to my hometown, I decided to run the first half at kamikaze pace and see what happened. What happened was a spectacular crash after 25km, a painful positive split, and a hard-earned lesson in marathon hubris.
- [Race to the Stones 2024: 100km Along Britain's Oldest Road](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/race-to-the-stones-2024): My first Race to the Stones—100km along Britain's oldest road. Struggled in the midday heat, ran strong in the second half. The ridiculously well-stocked aid stations and complete lack of mandatory kit made this feel more like a supported adventure than a race.
- [Cape Wrath Ultra Day 4: Finding My Rhythm in the Scottish Highlands](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/cape-wrath-ultra-day-4-2024): Day 4 of the Cape Wrath Ultra - cooler weather, runnable sections, and finding my rhythm after struggling on Day 3. Plus midges. Lots of midges.
- [UTMB OCC 2024: Chasing My Wife's Time Through the Alps](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/utmb-occ-2024): Ran the UTMB OCC 55km race with one mission: beat Victoria's time from last year of 11:25. The brutal heat made Col de Balme absolutely punishing. Finished in 11:39:17. I didn't beat Victoria. She's never going to let me forget it.
- [Winter on the Downs 2024: Running Through Storm Darragh](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/winter-on-the-downs-2024-storm-darragh): Completed the UK Ultra Winter on the Downs during Storm Darragh—the fiercest storm since Storm Eunice. Gale force winds, driving sideways rain, and moments where we were literally blown backwards. Finished in 11:41:04 and loved every terrifying minute.
- [Hurtwood 50k 2025: Mud, Rain, and a Mandatory Kit Error](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/hurtwood-50k-2025): Completed the Hurtwood 50k in 6:57:51—just scraping under seven hours. Pouring rain, howling wind, treacherous mud, and a rookie mandatory kit error when I forgot my water bottles. A fellow runner saved my race by lending me one.
- [Race to the Stones 2025: Running Happy on Britain's Oldest Road](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/race-to-the-stones-2025): Returned to Race to the Stones for a second year, deliberately running slower to enjoy the day. Finished in 15 hours 36 minutes on Britain's most ancient trail. Sometimes running happy beats running fast.
- [Manchester Marathon 2025: When It's Not Your Day](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/manchester-marathon-2025): Manchester Marathon 2025 - the biggest day of marathon running in UK history. I arrived not believing in myself and capitulated spectacularly in the second half. Finished in 3:40:48. Sometimes it's just not your day.
- [Lakeland 100 2022: How Hard Can It Be?](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/montane-lakeland-100-2022): My first Lakeland 100 attempt. I targeted sub-30 hours and finished in 34:36:56 with rotting feet. "It's only 100 miles - how hard can it be?" Famous last words.
- [Brighton Marathon 2025: Just Show Up](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/brighton-marathon-2025): Completed my 165th marathon and second Brighton in 3:59:56. Started as a pacer for friends but ended up running solo after the heat got to them. A philosophical run about why we keep coming back to 26.2 miles.
- [Race to the King 2025: A Lesson in Going Off Too Fast](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/race-to-the-king-2025): Finished Race to the King 2025 in 15 hours 10 minutes after going off far too fast, forgetting anti-chafe cream, and paying the price in the brutal heat. A timely bout of rain saved the day, but the damage was done. A lesson in race management.
- [Weald Challenge 50k 2016 | Getting Lost in Ashdown Forest](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/weald-challenge-50k-2016): A sunny 50k through the Ashdown Forest with friends – three weeks after Transvulcania. Getting lost twice despite GPS, volunteer appreciation, and finishing in 5:19:30.
- [Running Paris and Portsmouth](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/running-paris-and-portsmouth): I am continuing with my running and fundraising. I have four races coming up over the next few months and raising money in two of them.

- [South Downs Way 100 2024: The 500 Buckle](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/south-downs-way-100-2024): My 5th South Downs Way 100 finish and the 500 buckle - achieved against all odds with an injury from Cape Wrath and exhaustion from commentating the backyard ultra.
- [London Marathon 2024: Getting What I Deserved](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/london-marathon-2024): My 6th London Marathon, but with training decimated by illness. I got out exactly what I put in - a humbling reminder that there's no good or bad luck in marathon running.
- [Brighton Marathon 2024: Paul's First Sub-4](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/brighton-marathon-2024): My first Brighton Marathon after 12 years of running marathons, pacing Paul to his first sub-4 hour finish with our Zwift gang. Fat Boy Slim even showed up to cheer us on.
- [Ben Nevis Ultra 2022: Third Time Lucky](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/ben-nevis-ultra-2022): Third attempt at one of Britain's toughest 50km races. After two DNFs, I finally crossed the finish line - saved by extended cutoffs and a stubborn refusal to give up on the CMD Arete.
- [Marathon Madness Day 5 | Five in Five (or One for the Lazy)](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/marathon-madness-day-5-2018): Marathon Madness: five marathons in five days for the brave, one for the lazy. Eight laps on the beach at Lancing, finishing in darkness. Tim had 255 marathons before Monday. I had ice lollies.
- [South Downs Way 100 2023: The Hottest Day](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/south-downs-way-100-2023): Victoria's second 100-miler on the hottest South Downs Way 100 in memory. Both of us throwing up from mile 50, finishing 42 minutes inside the cutoff.
- [Paris Marathon 2023: Finally Breaking Three Hours](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/paris-marathon-2023-breaking-three-hours): After years of chasing it, I finally broke three hours at my 11th Paris Marathon. 2:55:44—a new PB, a London qualifier, and the culmination of a winter of hard training.
- [Trans Gran Canaria 2025: Chasing Cutoffs in the Canary Islands](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/trans-gran-canaria-2025): My third attempt at the Trans Gran Canaria Classic - 126km with 6,000m of climbing. - [Southend Pier Marathon 2018: The Longest Pier in the World](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/southend-pier-marathon-2018): A marathon on the longest pleasure pier in the world. Ten laps of Southend Pier, wristbands at every turn, and a sub-3:30 finish in the March wind.
- [Swiss Alps 100 2025: Two Attempts, Two DNFs](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/swiss-alps-100-2025): Second attempt at the Swiss Alps 100 in Switzerland. Made it all the way to the top of Breithorn at 2,500m before my stomach completely gave out. Arrived 10 minutes over cutoff after throwing up repeatedly on the final climb. The mountains won again.
- [Trans Gran Canaria 2022 | When Paradise Turned to Ice](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/trans-gran-canaria-2022-when-paradise-turned-to-ice): My second Trans Gran Canaria became a survival exercise when brutal weather hit the mountains. 125km with 6000m of climbing, freezing rain, and howling winds - one of the hardest races I've ever finished.
- [UTMB CCC 2018 | My First Taste of Mont Blanc](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/utmb-ccc-2018-first-taste-of-mont-blanc): My first UTMB event - 101km around Mont Blanc with 6,000m of climbing. A brutal lesson in humility as I scraped under 24 hours by just three minutes.
- [Royal Wedding and running](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/royal-wedding-and-running): The wedding of William and Kate took place a couple of weeks ago which was considered to be one of the best event insurance wedding ever in this year. I had to work but there was a street party on o...
- [Ridgeway Challenge 2025: 140km on Britain's Oldest Road](https://filmmyrun.com/blog/ridgeway-challenge-2025): Completed the full 140km Ridgeway Trail from Ivinghoe Beacon to Avebury Stone Circle in 24 hours 23 minutes. Struggled in the heat, survived on ice bandanas and power naps, then found my legs in the final 10km to secure 3rd place V55 at the British Trail Running Championships.

- [Swiss Alps 100 | In the Footsteps of my Great Uncle](https://filmmyrun.com/films/swiss-alps-100-great-uncle): A 100km ultra through the Swiss Alps, running past the Matterhorn — the mountain my great uncle Edward Whymper was the first to climb in 1865, in an ascent wher
- [Ben Nevis Ultra 2022 | Third Time Lucky?](https://filmmyrun.com/films/ben-nevis-ultra-2022): Timed out in 2019. Unfinished business in 2021. The Ben Nevis Ultra has beaten me twice — can I finally reach the finish?

- [Transgrancanaria 128km | Toughest One Yet?](https://filmmyrun.com/films/transgrancanaria-2020): A night start on Las Palmas beach, 128km across the volcanic island of Gran Canaria, and a camera that ran out of memory at the worst possible moment.

- [Grim Reaper Ultra 70 | Swimming, Vomiting, and Winning](https://filmmyrun.com/films/grim-reaper-ultra-2015): The 70-mile Grim Reaper Ultra at Grimsthorpe Castle — where Richard and I ran our first ultra together, went swimming in the lake, and somehow won.

- [South Downs Way 100 | Our First 100 Miler](https://filmmyrun.com/films/south-downs-way-100-first): The race that changed everything — my first ever 100-mile ultra marathon. Running through the night across the South Downs with my best mate Richard.

- [Jurassic Coast Challenge | Three Marathons in Three Days](https://filmmyrun.com/films/jurassic-coast-challenge-2017): Three consecutive marathons along the Jurassic Coast — a UNESCO World Heritage Site of dramatic cliffs, fossil beaches, and relentless hills.
- [Val d'Aran by UTMB | 100 Miles in the Pyrenees](https://filmmyrun.com/films/val-daran-100-utmb): 100 miles and 10,000 metres of ascent in the Pyrenees — the gnarliest terrain, a 48-hour cutoff, and an automatic entry to the UTMB 100.
